Let the first term be \(a\) and the common ratio \(r\).
\(t_4 = ar^3 = 48\) and \(t_8 = ar^7 = 768\).
Dividing, \(r^4 = \frac{768}{48} = 16\), so \(r^2 = 4\) and hence \(r^6 = \left(r^2\right)^3 = 64\).
\(t_{10} = ar^9 = \left(ar^3\right)r^6 = 48 \times 64\)
Hence the tenth term is \(3072\).

\(t_7 = ar^6\), so \(\frac{4}{3}r^6 = \frac{243}{1024}\).
\(r^6 = \frac{243}{1024} \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{729}{4096} = \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^6\)
The index 6 is even, so both signs satisfy this equation.
Hence \(r = \pm\frac{3}{4}\); the book records the positive value \(r = \frac{3}{4}\).

\(\frac{t_{n+1}}{t_n} = \frac{5^{n-1}}{7^{n-2}} \times \frac{7^{n-3}}{5^{n-2}} = 5^{(n-1)-(n-2)} \times 7^{(n-3)-(n-2)} = \frac{5}{7}\)
This ratio is the same constant for every \(n\), so the sequence is a G.P.
Putting \(n = 1\): \(t_1 = \frac{5^{-1}}{7^{-2}} = \frac{49}{5}\).
Hence the sequence is a G.P. with \(a = \frac{49}{5}\) and \(r = \frac{5}{7}\).

Take the three numbers as \(\frac{a}{r},\ a,\ ar\), so that the product is simply \(a^3\).
Product: \(a^3 = 1000\), so \(a = 10\).
Sum: \(10\left(\frac{1}{r} + 1 + r\right) = 35 \Rightarrow \frac{1}{r} + r = \frac{5}{2} \Rightarrow 2r^2 - 5r + 2 = 0\)
\((2r - 1)(r - 2) = 0\), so \(r = 2\) or \(r = \frac{1}{2}\).
Hence the numbers are \(5, 10, 20\) or \(20, 10, 5\).

Take the five numbers as \(\frac{a}{r^2},\ \frac{a}{r},\ a,\ ar,\ ar^2\), so that the product is \(a^5\).
Product: \(a^5 = 243\), so \(a = 3\).
Second \(+\) fourth: \(\frac{a}{r} + ar = 10 \Rightarrow 3\left(\frac{1}{r} + r\right) = 10 \Rightarrow 3r^2 - 10r + 3 = 0\)
\((3r - 1)(r - 3) = 0\), so \(r = 3\) or \(r = \frac{1}{3}\).
Hence the numbers are \(\frac{1}{3},\ 1,\ 3,\ 9,\ 27\) or \(27,\ 9,\ 3,\ 1,\ \frac{1}{3}\).

For \(n \ge 2\), \(t_n = S_n - S_{n-1} = 4\left(7^n - 1\right) - 4\left(7^{n-1} - 1\right) = 4\left(7^n - 7^{n-1}\right)\)
\(= 4 \cdot 7^{n-1}(7 - 1) = 24 \cdot 7^{n-1}\)
Also \(t_1 = S_1 = 4(7 - 1) = 24\), which is what this formula gives at \(n = 1\), so \(t_n = 24 \cdot 7^{n-1}\) for every \(n\).
Then \(\frac{t_{n+1}}{t_n} = \frac{24 \cdot 7^{n}}{24 \cdot 7^{n-1}} = 7\), the same for all \(n\).
Hence the sequence is a G.P. with \(a = 24\) and \(r = 7\).

The terms are not in G.P., so first write each digit-string in terms of powers of 10.
\(2 + 22 + 222 + \ldots = \frac{2}{9}\left(9 + 99 + 999 + \ldots\right) = \frac{2}{9}\sum_{k=1}^{n}\left(10^k - 1\right)\)
\(= \frac{2}{9}\left[\left(10 + 10^2 + \ldots + 10^n\right) - n\right] = \frac{2}{9}\left[\frac{10\left(10^n - 1\right)}{9} - n\right]\)
Hence the sum to \(n\) terms is \(\frac{2}{81}\left[10\left(10^n - 1\right) - 9n\right]\).

The \(n^{\text{th}}\) term is the decimal with \(n\) sixes, so
\(t_n = 6\left(\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{10^2} + \ldots + \frac{1}{10^n}\right)\), a G.P. with \(a = \frac{1}{10}\) and \(r = \frac{1}{10}\).
\(t_n = 6 \times \frac{\frac{1}{10}\left(1 - \frac{1}{10^n}\right)}{1 - \frac{1}{10}} = \frac{6}{9}\left(1 - \frac{1}{10^n}\right)\)
Hence \(t_n = \frac{2}{3}\left(1 - \frac{1}{10^n}\right)\).

\(\sum_{r=1}^{n}\left(5r^2 + 4r - 3\right) = 5\sum r^2 + 4\sum r - 3\sum 1\)
\(= 5 \cdot \frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6} + 4 \cdot \frac{n(n+1)}{2} - 3n\)
\(= \frac{n}{6}\left[5(n+1)(2n+1) + 12(n+1) - 18\right] = \frac{n}{6}\left[10n^2 + 15n + 5 + 12n + 12 - 18\right]\)
Hence the sum is \(\frac{n}{6}\left(10n^2 + 27n - 1\right)\).

Expand the general term first: \(r(r-3)(r-2) = r\left(r^2 - 5r + 6\right) = r^3 - 5r^2 + 6r\).
\(\sum_{r=1}^{n}\left(r^3 - 5r^2 + 6r\right) = \left[\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right]^2 - 5 \cdot \frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6} + 6 \cdot \frac{n(n+1)}{2}\)
\(= \frac{n(n+1)}{12}\left[3n(n+1) - 10(2n+1) + 36\right] = \frac{n(n+1)}{12}\left[3n^2 + 3n - 20n - 10 + 36\right]\)
Hence the sum is \(\frac{n(n+1)\left(3n^2 - 17n + 26\right)}{12}\).

The first factors \(2, 4, 6, \ldots\) are \(2r\) and the second factors \(6, 9, 12, \ldots\) are \(3(r+1)\).
\(t_r = 2r \cdot 3(r+1) = 6\left(r^2 + r\right)\)
\(\sum_{r=1}^{n}t_r = 6\left[\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6} + \frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right] = n(n+1)\left[(2n+1) + 3\right]\)
Hence the sum is \(6\left[\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6} + \frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right] = 2n(n+1)(n+2)\).

The three factors of the \(r^{\text{th}}\) term are \(2r,\ 2r+3,\ 2r+6\) (at \(r = 1\) these give \(2 \times 5 \times 8\)).
\(t_r = 2r(2r+3)(2r+6) = 2r\left(4r^2 + 18r + 18\right) = 8r^3 + 36r^2 + 36r\)
\(\sum_{r=1}^{n}t_r = 8\left[\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right]^2 + 36 \cdot \frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6} + 36 \cdot \frac{n(n+1)}{2}\)
\(= 2n(n+1)\left[n(n+1) + 3(2n+1) + 9\right] = 2n(n+1)\left(n^2 + 7n + 12\right)\)
Hence the sum is \(2n(n+1)(n+3)(n+4)\).

The \(r^{\text{th}}\) term is \(\frac{1^2 + 2^2 + \ldots + r^2}{r} = \frac{r(r+1)(2r+1)}{6r} = \frac{(r+1)(2r+1)}{6} = \frac{2r^2 + 3r + 1}{6}\).
\(\sum_{r=1}^{n}t_r = \frac{1}{6}\left[2 \cdot \frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6} + 3 \cdot \frac{n(n+1)}{2} + n\right]\)
\(= \frac{n}{36}\left[2(n+1)(2n+1) + 9(n+1) + 6\right] = \frac{n}{36}\left[4n^2 + 6n + 2 + 9n + 9 + 6\right]\)
Hence the sum is \(\frac{n\left(4n^2 + 15n + 17\right)}{36}\).

The sum starts at \(12^2\), so subtract the first eleven squares from the first twenty.
\(12^2 + 13^2 + \ldots + 20^2 = \sum_{r=1}^{20}r^2 - \sum_{r=1}^{11}r^2\)
\(= \frac{20 \times 21 \times 41}{6} - \frac{11 \times 12 \times 23}{6} = 2870 - 506\)
Hence the sum is \(2364\).

Each bracket is a difference of squares, \(a^2 - b^2 = (a+b)(a-b)\), and here \(a - b = 1\), so every bracket reduces to \(a + b\).
The expression \(= (50 + 49) + (48 + 47) + \ldots + (2 + 1) = 1 + 2 + 3 + \ldots + 50\)
\(= \frac{50 \times 51}{2}\)
Hence the value is \(1275\).

Numerator: \(t_r = r(2r+1) = 2r^2 + r\), so its sum is \(\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{3} + \frac{n(n+1)}{2} = \frac{n(n+1)(4n+5)}{6}\).
Denominator \(= \left[\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right]^2 = \frac{n^2(n+1)^2}{4}\).
\(\frac{n(n+1)(4n+5)}{6} \times \frac{4}{n^2(n+1)^2} = \frac{2(4n+5)}{3n(n+1)} = \frac{5}{9}\)
\(18(4n+5) = 15n(n+1) \Rightarrow 15n^2 - 57n - 90 = 0 \Rightarrow 5n^2 - 19n - 30 = 0\)
\((n - 5)(5n + 6) = 0\), and \(n\) must be a positive integer.
Hence \(n = 5\).

\(t_2 = ar = 7\) and \(t_4 = ar^3 = 1575\).
Dividing, \(r^2 = \frac{1575}{7} = 225\), so \(r = 15\) (taking the positive ratio).
\(a = \frac{7}{r} = \frac{7}{15}\)
Hence \(a = \frac{7}{15}\); with \(r = -15\) the first term would be \(-\frac{7}{15}\).

\(t_3 = ar^2 = \frac{1}{3}\) and \(t_6 = ar^5 = \frac{1}{81}\).
Dividing, \(r^3 = \frac{1}{81} \times 3 = \frac{1}{27}\).
A real cube root is unique, so no second sign arises here.
Hence \(r = \frac{1}{3}\).

The terms \(\frac{2}{3},\ \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2,\ \ldots,\ \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^n\) form a G.P. with \(a = \frac{2}{3}\) and \(r = \frac{2}{3}\).
\(S_n = \frac{\frac{2}{3}\left(1 - \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^n\right)}{1 - \frac{2}{3}} = \frac{2}{3} \times 3 \times \left(1 - \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^n\right)\)
Hence \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^r = 2\left[1 - \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^n\right]\).

For three consecutive terms of a G.P., the square of the middle term equals the product of the outer two.
\(k^2 = (k-1)(k+2) = k^2 + k - 2\)
\(k - 2 = 0\)
Hence \(k = 2\), and the terms are \(1, 2, 4\), a G.P. with \(r = 2\).

\(a = 27^2 = 729\) and \(t_7 = ar^6 = 8^2 = 64\).
\(r^6 = \frac{64}{729} = \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^6\), so take \(r = \frac{2}{3}\).
\(S_8 = \frac{729\left(1 - \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^8\right)}{1 - \frac{2}{3}} = 729 \times 3 \times \left(1 - \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^8\right)\)
Hence \(S_8 = 2187\left[1 - \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^8\right] = \frac{6305}{3}\).

Let the G.P. have first term \(A\) and common ratio \(R\), so \(x = AR^{p-1}\), \(y = AR^{q-1}\), \(z = AR^{r-1}\).
Index of \(A\): \((q-r) + (r-p) + (p-q) = 0\).
Index of \(R\): \((p-1)(q-r) + (q-1)(r-p) + (r-1)(p-q)\)
\(= (pq - pr + qr - pq + pr - qr) - \left[(q-r) + (r-p) + (p-q)\right] = 0 - 0 = 0\)
So \(x^{q-r} \cdot y^{r-p} \cdot z^{p-q} = A^0R^0\).
Hence the value is \(1\).

Inserting two terms between 5 and 40 gives a G.P. of four terms \(5,\ 5r,\ 5r^2,\ 40\).
\(5r^3 = 40 \Rightarrow r^3 = 8 \Rightarrow r = 2\)
The inserted terms are \(5r = 10\) and \(5r^2 = 20\).
Hence the two terms are \(10\) and \(20\).

Let \(p^{1/x} = q^{1/y} = r^{1/z} = k\). Then \(p = k^x\), \(q = k^y\) and \(r = k^z\).
Since \(p, q, r\) are in G.P., \(q^2 = pr\), so \(k^{2y} = k^{x+z}\).
Equating the indices, \(2y = x + z\), that is \(y - x = z - y\).
Hence \(x, y, z\) are in A.P.

Since \(a, b, c\) are in G.P., \(b^2 = ac\).
For \(ax^2 + 2bx + c = 0\) the discriminant is \((2b)^2 - 4ac = 4\left(b^2 - ac\right) = 0\), so this equation has the repeated root \(x = -\frac{2b}{2a} = -\frac{b}{a}\).
A root common to both equations must therefore be \(x = -\frac{b}{a}\), and it satisfies \(px^2 + 2qx + r = 0\):
\(p \cdot \frac{b^2}{a^2} + 2q\left(-\frac{b}{a}\right) + r = 0\)
Multiplying throughout by \(a^2\) gives \(pb^2 - 2qba + ra^2 = 0\), as was to be verified.

Let the common ratio be \(k\), so \(q = pk\), \(r = pk^2\), \(s = pk^3\).
L.H.S. \(= p^2\left(1 + k^2 + k^4\right) \times p^2k^2\left(1 + k^2 + k^4\right) = p^4k^2\left(1 + k^2 + k^4\right)^2\)
R.H.S. \(= \left(p^2k + p^2k^3 + p^2k^5\right)^2 = \left[p^2k\left(1 + k^2 + k^4\right)\right]^2 = p^4k^2\left(1 + k^2 + k^4\right)^2\)
The two sides are identical.
Hence \(\left(p^2 + q^2 + r^2\right)\left(q^2 + r^2 + s^2\right) = (pq + qr + rs)^2\).

Let the common ratio be \(k\), so \(q = pk\), \(r = pk^2\), \(s = pk^3\).
\(p^n + q^n = p^n\left(1 + k^n\right)\)
\(q^n + r^n = p^nk^n + p^nk^{2n} = p^nk^n\left(1 + k^n\right)\)
\(r^n + s^n = p^nk^{2n} + p^nk^{3n} = p^nk^{2n}\left(1 + k^n\right)\)
Each expression is \(k^n\) times the one before it, and \(\left(q^n + r^n\right)^2 = p^{2n}k^{2n}\left(1 + k^n\right)^2 = \left(p^n + q^n\right)\left(r^n + s^n\right)\).
Hence \(p^n + q^n,\ q^n + r^n,\ r^n + s^n\) are in G.P. with common ratio \(k^n\).

\(e^{2x} = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(2x)^n}{n!} = 1 + \frac{2x}{1!} + \frac{(2x)^2}{2!} + \ldots\)
The term containing \(x^6\) is \(\frac{(2x)^6}{6!} = \frac{64}{720}x^6\).
Hence the coefficient of \(x^6\) is \(\frac{64}{720} = \frac{4}{45}\).

The numerators \(1, 4, 7, 10, 13, \ldots\) form an A.P. with \(a = 1\) and \(d = 3\), while the denominators supply the G.P. factor \(x = \frac{1}{5}\), so \(t_r = (3r - 2)\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^{r-1}\): an arithmetico-geometric series.
Since \(|x| < 1\), \(S_\infty = \frac{a}{1 - x} + \frac{dx}{(1 - x)^2}\).
\(S_\infty = \frac{1}{1 - \frac{1}{5}} + \frac{3 \times \frac{1}{5}}{\left(1 - \frac{1}{5}\right)^2} = \frac{5}{4} + \frac{\frac{3}{5}}{\frac{16}{25}} = \frac{5}{4} + \frac{15}{16}\)
Hence \(S_\infty = \frac{35}{16}\).
